questions.q: A 35-year-old male presents with a well-defined erythematous plaque with central clearing on the trunk for 3 weeks. KOH mount shows septate hyphae with arthroconidia. Which organism is most likely responsible?
questions.exp: Trichophyton rubrum is the most common cause of tinea corporis in adults, showing septate hyphae on KOH. Microsporum canis is more common in children with scalp involvement. Candida causes intertrigo. Malassezia causes pityriasis versicolor.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman presents with a painless ulcer on the vulva. Dark-field microscopy of the lesion exudate shows motile spirochetes. The VDRL titre is 1:32. What is the most appropriate first-line treatment?
opts: Doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 14 days
Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM single dose
questions.exp: Primary syphilis is caused by Treponema pallidum. Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM is the first-line treatment per WHO/CDC guidelines. Doxycycline is used in penicillin-allergic patients. Azithromycin has emerging resistance.

questions.q: A 45-year-old farmer presents with multiple painless nodules along a lymphatic chain on the forearm, starting from a small inoculation wound on the hand. Biopsy shows asteroid bodies within suppurative granulomas. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Sporotrichosis (Sporothrix schenckii) classically presents with sporotrichoid spread - nodules along lymphatics following inoculation. Asteroid bodies (Splendore-Hoeppli phenomenon) are seen in the tissue. Leishmaniasis shows Leishman-Donovan bodies. Nocardia shows sulfur granules.

questions.q: A 22-year-old presents with hypopigmented anaesthetic patches on the trunk and thickened greater auricular nerve. Slit skin smear shows acid-fast bacilli in clumps (globi). Ridley-Jopling classification would place this patient in which category?
questions.exp: Lepromatous leprosy (LL) is characterised by multiple poorly-defined hypopigmented lesions, bilateral nerve thickening, and high bacterial load with globi (clumps of AFB) on smear. Tuberculoid leprosy has well-defined anaesthetic lesions and negative smear.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman on penicillamine for rheumatoid arthritis develops tense bullae on normal-looking skin with positive Nikolsky sign. Immunofluorescence shows IgG and C3 in a fishnet/reticular pattern along the basement membrane zone. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Drug-induced pemphigus vulgaris (penicillamine is the classic cause) shows positive Nikolsky sign (intraepidermal bulla) and IgG in a fishnet/intercellular pattern on DIF targeting desmoglein 3. Bullous pemphigoid shows linear IgG at BMZ. Linear IgA shows linear IgA at BMZ.

questions.q: A 30-year-old HIV-positive man presents with violaceous papules and nodules on the skin and hard palate. Biopsy shows spindle cell proliferation with slit-like vascular spaces and extravasated red blood cells. Which herpesvirus is implicated?
questions.exp: Kaposi's sarcoma is caused by HHV-8 (Human Herpesvirus 8 / KSHV). It classically occurs in HIV-positive men and shows violaceous vascular tumours. Histology shows spindle cells, slit-like vascular spaces, and PAS-positive hyaline globules.

questions.q: A 40-year-old woman presents with butterfly rash on the face, photosensitivity, oral ulcers, arthritis, and proteinuria. ANA is 1:640 with anti-dsDNA antibodies. Which skin finding in this patient confers the worst prognosis for renal involvement?
questions.exp: Palpable purpura indicating vasculitis in SLE is associated with immune complex deposition and correlates with renal and systemic disease severity. Discoid plaques are associated with lower likelihood of systemic involvement. Periungual telangiectasia is more typical of dermatomyositis.

questions.q: A 16-year-old boy presents with multiple comedones, papules, and nodular cysts on the face. He is being considered for isotretinoin therapy. Which of the following is an absolute contraindication?
questions.exp: Pregnancy is the only absolute contraindication to isotretinoin due to severe teratogenicity (craniofacial, cardiac, CNS abnormalities). Hypertriglyceridaemia is a relative contraindication and should be monitored. IBD is a relative contraindication due to possible exacerbation.

questions.q: A 60-year-old chronic smoker presents with a pearly, telangiectatic nodule on the nose that bleeds on minor trauma. Biopsy shows peripheral palisading of basaloid cells with retraction artifact. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma (nodular type) classically presents as a pearly papule/nodule with telangiectasia and rolled borders on sun-exposed skin. Histology shows peripheral palisading of basaloid cells and retraction artifact (shrinkage of stroma). It is the most common skin cancer.

questions.q: A 25-year-old man presents with grouped vesicles on an erythematous base on the buttock for 5 days with burning pain. He had a similar episode 3 months ago. Tzanck smear shows multinucleate giant cells. What is the most appropriate long-term management?
opts: Episodic valacyclovir 1 g twice daily for 10 days
Suppressive acyclovir 400 mg twice daily continuously
questions.exp: Recurrent genital herpes (HSV-2) with ≥6 episodes/year warrants suppressive therapy with acyclovir 400 mg BD or valacyclovir 500 mg OD. This reduces frequency, severity, and asymptomatic shedding. Episodic therapy is less effective for frequent recurrences.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman presents with thickened, sclerotic skin over the face and hands with Raynaud's phenomenon. ANA shows anticentromere antibody pattern. Which subtype of systemic sclerosis is she most likely suffering from?
questions.exp: Anticentromere antibody (ACA) is characteristic of limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis (lcSSc/CREST syndrome - Calcinosis, Raynaud's, Esophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly, Telangiectasia). Anti-Scl-70 (topoisomerase I) is associated with diffuse cutaneous SSc.

questions.q: A 3-year-old child presents with vesicles, bullae, and erosions on the flexures and periorificially. The mother has similar lesions. Immunofluorescence shows IgA deposition in a fishnet pattern in the epidermis. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Hailey-Hailey disease (familial benign chronic pemphigus) is an autosomal dominant condition caused by ATP2C1 mutation affecting calcium pump, leading to acantholysis. DIF shows IgA in intercellular spaces. It affects flexures. Chronic bullous disease of childhood shows linear IgA at BMZ.

questions.q: A 50-year-old man presents with an annular plaque with a raised, pearly border on the glans penis. Biopsy shows full-thickness dysplasia of the epithelium. What is the correct diagnosis?
questions.exp: Erythroplasia of Queyrat is squamous cell carcinoma in situ (Bowen's disease) occurring on the glans penis. It presents as a velvety, erythematous plaque and shows full-thickness epidermal dysplasia. Bowen's disease is the term used for the same condition on non-mucosal skin.

questions.q: A 45-year-old man with type I reaction of leprosy (reversal reaction) presents with acute neuritis. What is the treatment of choice?
questions.exp: Type 1 reaction (reversal reaction) is a delayed hypersensitivity reaction. Prednisolone (40-60 mg/day) is the treatment of choice and must be started promptly to prevent irreversible nerve damage. MDT should be continued. Thalidomide is used for Type 2 (ENL) reactions.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman presents with yellowish, waxy, well-circumscribed papules in the nasolabial folds, on the upper eyelids and oral mucosa. Biopsy reveals foamy histiocytes with a Touton giant cell pattern. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Xanthoma disseminatum (XD) is a non-Langerhans histiocytosis with normolipidaemic xanthomas involving skin, mucous membranes, and often the CNS and diabetes insipidus. Touton giant cells are characteristic. Xanthelasma is restricted to eyelids and associated with hyperlipidaemia.

questions.q: A 22-year-old man presents with target lesions on the palms and oral erosions developing 3 days after starting trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. Nikolsky sign is negative. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Erythema multiforme major (EMM) shows classic target lesions and mucosal involvement at <2 body surface areas. SJS shows widespread purpuric macules and ≥2 mucosal surfaces with BSA detachment <10%. TEN shows >30% BSA detachment. EM is often triggered by herpes, while SJS is drug-induced.

questions.q: A patient presents with recurrent painful oral ulcers, genital ulcers, uveitis, and a positive pathergy test. Which HLA type is strongly associated with this condition?
questions.exp: Behçet's disease is strongly associated with HLA-B51. It presents with recurrent oral and genital aphthous ulcers, uveitis, skin lesions, and positive pathergy test (pustule formation after needle prick). HLA-B27 is associated with ankylosing spondylitis.

questions.q: A 40-year-old man presents with scaly plaques on the elbows and knees and pitting of fingernails. He is started on methotrexate. Which blood test is most important to monitor before each cycle?
questions.exp: Complete blood count (CBC) is the most critical monitoring test before each methotrexate dose as it detects bone marrow suppression (leukopenia, thrombocytopenia). LFTs and renal function are monitored periodically (not before every dose). Folic acid supplementation reduces side effects.

questions.q: A 5-year-old child presents with honey-crusted erosions on the face spreading rapidly. Gram stain of the crust shows gram-positive cocci in clusters. What is the causative organism and its mechanism of action?
opts: Group A Streptococcus producing streptolysin O
Staphylococcus aureus producing exfoliative toxin A
Group A Streptococcus producing erythrogenic toxin
questions.exp: Impetigo contagiosa is caused by Staphylococcus aureus (predominantly) and sometimes GAS. Bullous impetigo is caused by S. aureus phage group 2 producing exfoliative toxin A (ETA) and B, which cleave desmoglein 1 causing intraepidermal splitting.

questions.q: A 32-year-old woman is being evaluated for dermoscopy. The lesion shows a brown-black network with abrupt cutoff at the periphery and irregular dots/globules. What dermoscopic feature most suggests malignant melanoma?
opts: Atypical pigment network with regression structures
Blue-white veil over area <25% of lesion
questions.exp: Atypical/irregular pigment network, regression structures (white scar-like areas + blue pepper-like granules), blue-white veil, irregular streaks/dots/globules are dermoscopic features of melanoma. Regular network and peripheral regular globules suggest benign melanocytic naevus.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman presents with disseminated gonococcal infection (DGI) with multiple pustular skin lesions on the extremities and asymmetric migratory polyarthritis. What is the most appropriate treatment?
opts: Penicillin G IV 10 million units daily for 7 days
Ceftriaxone 1 g IV/IM once daily for 7 days
Ciprofloxacin 500 mg orally twice daily for 14 days
questions.exp: Disseminated gonococcal infection is treated with ceftriaxone 1 g IV/IM once daily for 7 days (or until 24-48 hours after clinical improvement, then oral cefixime to complete 7 days). Due to increasing fluoroquinolone resistance, ciprofloxacin is no longer first-line.

questions.q: A 55-year-old man presents with violaceous papules on the wrists and oral white lacy lesions (Wickham's striae). Biopsy shows vacuolar degeneration of basal cells and a band-like lymphocytic infiltrate at the DEJ. What cells are predominantly involved in pathogenesis?
opts: B lymphocytes producing IgG against desmoglein
CD4+ Th2 cells producing IL-4 and IL-13
CD8+ cytotoxic T cells targeting basal keratinocytes
questions.exp: Lichen planus pathogenesis involves CD8+ cytotoxic T cells that recognize altered antigen on basal keratinocytes, leading to lichenoid tissue reaction with band-like infiltrate, vacuolar degeneration of basal cells, and Civatte bodies (apoptotic keratinocytes).

questions.q: A 70-year-old man presents with a slowly growing reddish-brown plaque on the preauricular area for 2 years with nodules developing within it. Biopsy shows atypical lymphocytes with cerebriform nuclei in the epidermis (Pautrier's microabscesses). What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Mycosis fungoides (cutaneous T-cell lymphoma) presents with patch, plaque, and tumour stages. Pautrier's microabscesses (atypical lymphocytes within epidermis) are pathognomonic. Cells are CD4+CD8- with cerebriform nuclei. Pagetoid reticulosis (Woringer-Kolopp) is a localized variant.

questions.q: A 28-year-old male presents with a single painless papule on the penis that ulcerates and heals, followed by bilateral inguinal lymphadenopathy with groove sign. Complement fixation test is positive at 1:64. What is the causative organism?
questions.exp: Lymphogranuloma venereum (LGV) is caused by Chlamydia trachomatis serovars L1, L2, L3. The groove sign (femoral and inguinal lymphadenopathy separated by inguinal ligament creating a groove) is pathognomonic. CFT >1:64 is diagnostic. Haemophilus ducreyi causes chancroid (painful ulcer).

questions.q: A 50-year-old diabetic man presents with woody, indurated plaques on the lower legs bilaterally with central atrophic yellowish areas and violaceous borders. Biopsy shows necrobiosis of collagen with palisading granulomas. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Necrobiosis lipoidica (NLD) presents on the pretibial region in diabetics as yellowish, waxy plaques with atrophic centers and telangiectasia, and violaceous borders. Histology shows palisading granulomas with necrobiosis. Granuloma annulare also shows necrobiosis but occurs on dorsal hands/feet.

questions.q: A 20-year-old woman presents with painful, erythematous nodules on the anterior shins for 10 days following sore throat. ESR is elevated and ASO titre is high. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Erythema nodosum presents as tender, erythematous, non-ulcerating nodules on the anterior shins, most commonly triggered by Streptococcal infection (elevated ASO). Other causes include TB, sarcoidosis, drugs (OCPs), IBD. Biopsy shows septal panniculitis without vasculitis.

questions.q: During Mohs micrographic surgery, the surgeon examines horizontal frozen sections. What is the key advantage of this technique over standard wide local excision for basal cell carcinoma?
opts: Complete margin evaluation with maximum tissue conservation
Lower cost and shorter operative time
Better cosmetic outcome due to grafting
questions.exp: Mohs micrographic surgery allows complete 100% margin examination of the excised tissue using horizontal sectioning (vs. bread-loaf vertical sectioning in standard excision which samples <1% of margins). This maximizes tissue conservation while ensuring complete tumour removal. Cure rates >99% for primary BCC.

questions.q: A 65-year-old man presents with scaling, fissuring plaques on bilateral palms for 6 months with no pruritus. KOH mount is negative. He is a chronic smoker. Biopsy shows hyperkeratosis, parakeratosis, and mild spongiosis without eosinophils. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Tylosis (hereditary palmoplantar keratoderma) presents with diffuse or focal hyperkeratosis of palms and soles. Acquired PPK can be associated with malignancy, drugs, or infections. The histology of non-inflammatory hyperkeratosis with parakeratosis is typical of PPK. KOH negative excludes tinea.

questions.q: A 30-year-old man presents with multiple flesh-colored papules on the penis and perianal region. The lesions show koilocytosis on biopsy. HPV typing reveals HPV 6 and 11. Which treatment is specifically contraindicated in pregnancy?
questions.exp: Podophyllin (podophyllotoxin) is absolutely contraindicated in pregnancy due to teratogenicity and systemic absorption causing fetal toxicity. It should also not be used on large surface areas. Cryotherapy and TCA are safe in pregnancy. Laser ablation may also be used in pregnancy.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman with dermatomyositis develops dysphagia and respiratory muscle weakness. Skin biopsy shows vacuolar degeneration of basal cells and perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate with mucin deposition. Which antibody is most specific for rapidly progressive ILD in dermatomyositis?
questions.exp: Anti-MDA5 (anti-melanoma differentiation-associated protein 5) antibody in dermatomyositis is strongly associated with rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease (RP-ILD) with high mortality, and often presents with clinically amyopathic dermatomyositis. Anti-TIF1-gamma is associated with malignancy.
